{{Short description|Theorem in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], the ''' Beurling–Lax theorem''' is a [[theorem]] due to {{harvtxt|Beurling|1948}} and {{harvtxt|Lax|1959}} which characterizes the [[shift operator|shift]]-[[invariant subspace|invariant]] subspaces of the [[Hardy space]] <math>H^2(\mathbb{D},\mathbb{C})</math>. It states that each such space is of the form

: <math> \theta H^2(\mathbb{D},\mathbb{C}), </math>

for some [[inner function]] <math>\theta</math>.

The result is a significant connection between [[operator theory]] with [[complex analysis]].
